what_this_is: an ADDITIVE annotation file beside legality_rules.json. It supersedes nothing and rewrites nothing: legality_rules.json is not touched, and no rule shape is edited. It names rule ids whose operand exclusion the owner has RATIFIED AS LEGAL, with the reason, so the validator can score a candidate covered by one of them as an agreement instead of a miss.

ruling.words: if c++ allows it and someone can use it with intention, its valid
ruling.consequence_stated_in_the_ruling: c++'s bool increment/decrement is LEGAL in the legality rules, annotated as a language quirk (deprecated-but-allowed), not a standing miss; the 4 validated-miss cases become 4 validated agreements

how_it_is_applied: a validation candidate scored predicted_legal_but_refused, whose misfired rule id set intersects the annotated ids below, is counted as agreement_by_ratified_quirk and listed separately with the compiler's own refusal text kept verbatim. The compiler's refusal is NOT erased and NOT contradicted: it is recorded as a flag-dependent deprecation diagnostic over a construct the language admits.
spelling_ban: the annotation is keyed by RULE ID -- the authority's own name for its check -- never by an operator token. The token appears only in the display `spelling` field of the unit objects the validator already carries.

annotations.note: clang's own diagnostic is an EXTENSION diagnostic (`ext_increment_bool`), which is a deprecation, not an absence of the operation. Under the ratified reading the operand shape is legal and the diagnostic records that the language deprecates it.
the decrement half of the same clang check. Ratified together with the increment half by the same ruling.
